_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. REPRINT 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey and the key-aware --fail-on scan natively in doctor.go (so doctor_verdict.go no longer defines them) and has dropped the 'but auth was accepted' line for a WARN. Still connector-only: refusing to dial the shipped placeholder base_url, the explicit ERROR row when no credential is configured, and doctorUnexpectedStatus (404 = wrong base_url, api row goes red). Also re-applied at the 4.32.5 review: the generated credential probe used the cache-enabled GetWithHeaders, so a credential revoked server-side could read 'valid' from a cached 200 for the cache TTL; doctor.go now calls GetWithHeadersNoCache. And doctorShippedBaseURL is EMPTY for huntress: https://api.huntress.io is the real, only API host, so an operator who never set HUNTRESS_BASE_URL is correctly configured - filling the literal in (v0.1.5 and earlier) made doctor refuse to probe every default install. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press now generates doctorBaseURLIsPlaceholder in doctor.go for literal unset values, so the connector's shipped-placeholder check is renamed doctorBaseURLIsShippedPlaceholder and doctor.go calls both.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For huntress the manifest gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. server.json gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: HUNTRESS_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press adds the runtime switches HUNTRESS_MCP_READ_ONLY (preset to 1 on every channel) and HUNTRESS_NO_LOCAL_DATA; both are declared on all three channels and pinned here.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so one client cannot hold it open by dribbling request headers
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.5 gives every MCP server a --transport http mode (streamable HTTP behind bearer auth) and the generated cmd/huntress-mcp/main.go http.Server literal sets no header-read deadline, so a single client could hold the listener open indefinitely by sending request headers one byte at a time (Slowloris). gosec G112 flags exactly this shape and the security gate raised it as P1 on the 4.32.5 reprint (same finding datagate carried since PR #317). The fix adds ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second to the http.Server literal. A reprint regenerates main.go without the field and go build stays green, so this marker is the only thing that notices. code_only because the explanatory comment above the field also names G112 - the assert must be satisfied by the field itself. DURABLE FIX belongs in the press's mcp main.go template; file via printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 2 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: accounts incident-reports post-v1-accounts-account-id-id-remediations-bulk-approval (POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/incident_reports/{incident_report_id}/remediations/bulk_approval); incident-reports remediations bulk-rejection-parameters (POST /v1/incident_reports/{incident_report_id}/remediations/bulk_rejection).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the title of an HTML page returned where JSON was expected. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts. Codex r2 success-body class (2026-10-24): every successful answer now passes one check, funnelSuccessBody -> successBodyRefused, on every path: each cached read (a refused entry is deleted and the call falls through to a checked live request), the live binary envelope as returned (its content_type header and its text, plus its decoded bytes), and the live JSON/text body; the response cache moved to resources-success-checked and the legacy resources dir an older build served unchecked is removed when a client binds its cache; a body over the funnel's 1 MiB cap fails closed (not JSON: refused; JSON: checked in the existing overlapping windows AND in windows cut only between tokens, so every key, string, number and literal is checked whole, and a token over the cap is refused). Issue #495 (2026-11-04): the funnel's work per byte grows with the length it reads, so a whole page of five or more ordinary incident reports spent the budget and was refused as an echo (0.1.11). Every JSON success body is now checked in windows of about 4 KiB cut only between tokens (successBodyTokensEcho with successFunnelWindow): every key, string, number and literal is still checked whole, 8-character pieces are still held, a token over the funnel cap still withholds, and a body that is not JSON is checked whole up to 1 MiB and refused over it. The raw overlapping windows are removed: they cut through tokens and spent the same budget.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: Local novels reconcile flat and reseller alias copies against completed sync snapshots and merged account identity; every list is read through one envelope parser; unreadable inputs are withheld as unknown, never published as 0; blast-radius parses address tokens.
handfixes.why: An MSP acts on these numbers (billing, coverage, incident triage). The union of alias copies resurrected rows a later complete sync removed and split one account into two billing groups (200 seats for 100); an HTTP 200 without the agents array read as zero deployed agents; a null EDR minimum still published minimum_usage_total 0; unreadable timestamps were bucketed as new, averaged away or silently skipped; blast-radius matched dotted names as substrings and missed other spellings of an address; a legacy sync_state silently skipped the completeness warning. Each class now fails closed: the right number, or the number withheld with a warning naming what could not be read. A reprint regenerates none of these hand-written novel files, but a re-onboard or replay that restores an older copy would bring every class back. Codex round 1 (2026-10-24): Codex r1 on fix B (fix C): a row is left out as removed upstream only when a FULL walk of its scope (from the first page in one run, to a proven natural end, with no --param/--global-param/--resource-param filter) recorded in the hand-written walk_coverage table (store/extras.go, written by five one-line sync.go call sites) started after the row was written; filtered, resumed, unfinished, scope-unknown and unrecorded later syncs keep the row, counted and named in a warning, and blast-radius's SQL prefilter is a superset of what the Go matcher accepts (IPv4-mapped IPv6, Unicode case variants, non-text array elements). Indicator class fix (2026-10-24, after the review budget stop): the --indicator argument and every stored-text token are read by one parser, parseAddressToken (label such as ip:/host:/mac:, brackets, port, IPv6 zone, IPv4-mapped prefix, dots at either end), so an indicator with a port matches the same address; a match that covers only part of an address the parser finds (including one after a label) is a fragment, never exact. Property tests: every accepted spelling used as the indicator matches a row holding any other spelling of the same address, through the command and its SQL prefilter; a partial address is never exact. SKILL.md lists the 13 tools HUNTRESS_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 removes, measured from tools/list.

handfixes.summary: Every CLI command that changes the Huntress tenant (endpoint commands whose pp:method is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, plus import) refuses before any client exists unless --yes or --dry-run is given; siem's read-only POST is the one allowlisted pp:path.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 P1: `huntress-cli accounts incident-reports post-v1-accounts-account-id-id-remediations-bulk-approval 4421 98765 --agent` POSTed approval of every pending remediation (Huntress then carries them out on hosts) with no confirmation, while the MCP twin huntress_execute already required confirm=true. The gate is one call in the root PersistentPreRunE (write_confirm_gate.go), fail-closed on the method annotation so a future generated write command is covered without an edit; the refusal is a usage error (exit 2) with a JSON envelope carrying confirmation_required under --json/--agent. A --yes saved in a run profile does not count. Help examples of gated commands are rewritten at tree build so none shows a refused invocation. A reprint that drops the root.go call leaves the gate file dead; write_confirm_gate_test.go drives every write command against a fake API and fails if any sends without --yes. The same commit corrects novel descriptions that claimed output the commands do not produce (coverage percent, posture grade, invoice totals, version changes, outdated EDR versions, per-org subscription reconciliation); root.go and which.go are generated, so those corrections are pinned here and the old strings are banned.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync treats a walk with no next cursor as finished when every page declared the same total_count (top level, or total_count/totalCount/total inside pagination/meta/paging/page_info) and the walk saw at least that many distinct record ids. Applied in the flat walk, its --max-pages branch and the per-parent dependent walk; the pagination_cursor_missing warning is suppressed in that case. A count-proven end is never evidence of absence: reconcile is skipped with reason end_proven_by_count, and walk_coverage does not record it as a full enumeration (flat, per parent and the fan-out aggregate).
handfixes.why: Huntress omits next_page_token on the last page, so a final page that is exactly full or an endpoint that returns every row in one page ended as cursor_unavailable: identities, reports and accounts_reports stayed incomplete with every row stored, and store_status read partial on every run (#709). Distinct ids and a stable count keep a duplicate row across pages or a count that moved mid-walk from certifying a truncated walk, which would let reconcile delete rows the API still has (Codex round 1). A reprint regenerates sync.go without the guard. Rows that shift pages under concurrent deletes and inserts can satisfy a stable count with distinct ids while a live row was skipped, so only the natural-end proofs authorize reconcile (Codex round 2). walk_coverage full_* records let drift and the reconciled views leave out rows a walk did not return, so they follow the same rule (Codex round 3).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should accept a declared total_count reached as a proven end that never authorizes a prune or a full walk record: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5390

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.
